findings.title: SLA filtering can return threads whose current status does not match
findings.failure: A thread with an older BREACHED next-response tracker and a newer PENDING one matches `slaStatuses: [BREACHED]`, although its returned summary says PENDING. Such threads also count toward `totalCount` and occupy page slots, so the tool cannot reliably answer a request for threads currently breached.
findings.fix: If the tool is meant to search current status, filter on the latest tracker for each thread and SLA type. Verify the behavior with a repeated next-response or total-resolution target.
findings.evidence: The new operation passes the variables to `serviceLevelAgreements`. `packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDbFilterUtils.ts:679` matches any tracker with `EXISTS`, while `packages/aggregates/src/service-level-agreement/serviceLevelAgreementTrackerAggregate.ts:390` supplies the latest tracker to the summary. The operation comments at lines 46–58 acknowledge this mismatch.

findings.title: Use file-local fragments for the repeated SLA detail selection
findings.failure: The same six status selections are repeated for four targets in each of three operations. A future field change can update one target while leaving the others with different output.
findings.fix: Define one fragment on `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail` in each operation file and spread it under all four targets.
findings.evidence: The repeated blocks start at `getThreadDetails.graphql:96`, `getThreads.graphql:174`, and `searchThreads.graphql:114`. `services/mcp-server/operations/duplicateBroadcast.graphql:96` documents and demonstrates the existing file-local fragment pattern.
